name: Deleting a Forest of Minimum Sections
statement: Let $M\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$ be maximum of rank $r$ and let $M[p_i]=\partial_{B_i}M$ be minimum sections. After deleting every word matching some $p_i$, the residual $C$ is nonempty and ample with $\operatorname{Sh}(C)=\{T:|T|\le r,\ B_i\nsubseteq T\text{ for all }i\}$. Join two patterns when they disagree on their overlap. If this disagreement graph is a forest, $C$ has a rank-$r$ parent with at most $\sum_i\max(r+1-|B_i|,0)$ auxiliaries, preserving any disjoint old mark.
proof: Incompatible minimum patterns have union support at least $r+2$ and their deleted sections are disjoint. Inclusion--exclusion matches the residual word count with the displayed support family, so the sandwich theorem gives ampleness and exact shattering. For the parent, repeatedly choose a leaf of the disagreement forest. A modified predecessor construction preserves all compatible minima and the leaf's sole possible incompatible neighbor. The single-section lift deletes the leaf in the stated number of steps without changing the disagreement graph; induction over leaves completes the construction.
comments: The shattering formula does not require the forest hypothesis. Cyclic disagreement families are not covered by the parent construction. Properness of the supplied maximum class is essential.
